banoffee-pie|required-wait-not-counted|L.problem: The method heated a sealed can, which the manufacturer of the best-known condensed milk advises against for safety, and the cooling before opening was untimed and uncounted.
banoffee-pie|required-wait-not-counted|L.action: Replaced with the manufacturer's open-dish method: the milk poured into a pie dish, covered with foil, baked in a water bath at 220°C / 425°F for 1 to 1½ hours until thick and caramel-coloured, then whisked; ready-made caramel offered as the no-cook alternative. The ingredient line now gives 397 g so the nutrition can read it (tier 3 to tier 2). The base is made and chilled while the toffee bakes. Cook 60 to 90 minutes (was 180). The toffee cooling is declared untimed with a readiness cue (barely warm and spreadable). Why, tips, description, search description and one keyword ("no bake british dessert", no longer true) updated.
banoffee-pie|required-wait-not-counted|L.source: Eagle Brand (Smucker's), Product FAQs: "For safety reasons, we do not recommend heating a can of our condensed milk, opened or unopened. The current can is not designed to withstand high temperatures." Its caramel recipe pages give the oven (pie plate, foil, water bath, 425°F, 1 to 1½ hours), double-boiler and microwave methods and end "CAUTION: NEVER HEAT UNOPENED CAN." https://www.eaglebrand.com/eagle-brand-product-faqs/
banoffee-pie|required-wait-not-counted|L.limitation: The oven time comes from the manufacturer for its product; a UK tin (Carnation) is the same weight, and no UK manufacturer statement was found. Cooling time is not stated.
